goal: Agent apps that pin profiles admit a turn without re-reading what the caller read under its lock; Hospitality first words server-side p90 <= 4.0 s per channel
lever: readProfileAdmission returns an opaque handle (prior pin, binding, pinned revision by id); admitProfileTurn accepts only an issued handle and skips re-reading pin and binding; the active-revision pointer stays a live read; the pin write still compare-and-sets on binding.version
hypothesis: Hospitality prepared->admitted (~240 ms warm, ~215 ms new chat, H4 d2bb4e3) is mostly admitProfileTurn re-reading turn pin, binding and revision in series after the caller already read them.

measurement.selection: 4 turns sent in one existing chat on ws-2621b7ba at 00:28Z (turns 2-5 of the same-chat run)

calibration.next: compare with tangle-ops trace-stats --entry hospitality for the same turnIds

prediction.channels: every channel of every app that pins profiles (web chat, guest web, lines)

lever: admission read token (review fixes: opaque token, WeakMap data, single use)
correction: Per independent review: the saving exists only when the caller swaps its own pin and binding reads for readProfileAdmission. Per path: old admitProfileTurn = 3 serial reads + pinTurn; with a token = 1 live active read (0 when the revision is pinned) + pinTurn, while readProfileAdmission costs 1 parallel round (pin with binding) + 1 when pinned. Hospitality replaces its post-lock binding re-check with readProfileAdmission (read after recordSwitch on a new chat), so its net saving is about 2 serial round trips. Library-only adoption without that swap saves nothing.

prediction.condition: Hospitality adopts the token in place of its own post-lock binding re-check
